title: Edit Mode: extrude a face
summary: Switch the cube into Edit Mode, select its top face and pull it upward with Extrude.

steps.say: In Object Mode, click the cube in the 3D viewport so it gets an orange outline.

checks.prompt: Is the cube in the 3D viewport outlined in orange, showing it is selected?

hints: You can also click Cube in the Outliner at the top right.
No cube in the scene? Press Shift A, then Mesh, then Cube.
steps.why: Edit Mode works on the selected object.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, press Tab to switch to Edit Mode.

checks.prompt: Does the mode selector at the top left of the viewport now read Edit Mode, with the cube's vertices and edges visible?

hints: The header should change from Object Mode to Edit Mode.
Or open the mode selector at the top left of the viewport and pick Edit Mode.
steps.why: Edit Mode lets you change the shape itself, not only move the whole object.

steps.say: Press 3 on the number row above the letters to switch to face select.

checks.prompt: In the viewport header, is the face select button, the third of the three small square icons next to Edit Mode, highlighted?

hints: Use the 3 above the E key, not the one on the numpad.
Or click the third of the three small icons right of the Edit Mode selector.
steps.why: Face select lets you pick whole faces with one click.

steps.say: Press Alt A to clear the current selection.

checks.prompt: Is the cube now shown with no orange highlighted faces?

hints: Hold Alt, tap A, and let go.
Or open the Select menu in the viewport header and choose None.
steps.why: Starting from an empty selection makes sure only one face gets extruded.

steps.say: Click the top face of the cube. It turns orange.

checks.prompt: Is exactly one face, the top of the cube, highlighted in orange?

hints: Click near the middle of the top surface, where the face dot is.
Cannot see the top? Hold the middle mouse button and drag to orbit until it faces you.
steps.why: Extrude works on whatever faces are selected.

steps.say: Press E and move the mouse up to pull the face out of the cube. Click to confirm.

checks.prompt: Is the cube now taller, with new side faces between the original top and the raised face?

hints: The face follows the mouse until you click. Right-click cancels the move.
For an exact height, press E, type 1, and press Enter. Control Z undoes the extrude.
steps.why: Extrude adds new geometry, so you can grow shapes out of a simple cube.

steps.say: Press Tab again to go back to Object Mode.

checks.prompt: Does the mode selector at the top left of the viewport read Object Mode again?

hints: Keep the mouse over the 3D viewport when you press Tab.
Or pick Object Mode from the mode selector at the top left of the viewport.
steps.why: Object Mode is where you arrange, shade and render finished objects.
